objective: Extend the cloud System quest model into backward-compatible Quest v2 with structured objectives/progress, deadlines, hidden/reveal, explicit failure/expiry and a hard MAX_ACTIVE_PLAYER_QUESTS=1 focus invariant, while preserving the same append-only ledger, calibrated reward/evidence rules and legacy Quest v1 history.

roles_before.artifact: Ron OS and claim-specific live owners own real-world facts/execution; System quest state is derived only.
Neon/PostgreSQL system_events is the sole mutable derived-state owner.
system_apply_action(...) is the shared PostgreSQL mutation gate for HTTP and authorized ChatGPT writes.
Existing Quest v1 events remain valid historical events; the lingering persist-probe is legacy infrastructure residue, not a player-focus quest.
Ron explicitly requires at most one ACTIVE real/player quest at a time so attention is not scattered; technical/infrastructure probes must not consume that slot.
Scored quest reward amounts are constrained by system-quest-reward:v1; progression requires a verified completion basis and one basis can reward once.
Exact action retries replay and conflicting idempotency-key reuse is rejected.
Northflank PWA reads the same event-derived snapshot and renders quest state.
ChatGPT is the sole intended interactive System controller under skills/system-controller.md.
LifeUp bridge code remains legacy/rollback evidence and is outside the target runtime.
PROTOCOL.md exact live-mutation permission gate remains authoritative; candidate work must not silently mutate production player/schema state.

role_dispositions.destination: Quest progress/completion evidence remains derived and cannot overwrite stronger real-world owners.
All Quest v2 lifecycle changes are append-only events in system_events; no parallel quest store is added.
system_apply_action remains the single public gate; migration 005 adds Quest v2 lifecycle and migration 006 adds the player-focus slot guard while preserving an internal v1 fallback.
Old Quest v1 events project under the old contract. Legacy v1 infrastructure probes do not consume the Quest v2 player-focus slot.

Every new Quest v2 is a player quest. At most one Quest v2 may be ACTIVE globally. COMPLETE/CANCEL/FAIL/EXPIRE frees the slot. No client-controlled technical bypass exists; future infrastructure probes must not be represented as Quest v2 player quests.
Quest v2 does not change system-quest-reward:v1 or progression award amounts/basis rules.
All new actions flow through the existing idempotency contract and append-only ledger.
PWA renders structured objectives/progress/deadline/rewards, suppresses unrevealed hidden quests and uses level-local XP progress; it remains projection-only.
ChatGPT remains sole intended interactive controller and selects/operates the one player-focus quest using authoritative context.
No legacy LifeUp runtime file is required or modified by Quest v2.
Candidate code/tests may be built safely, but promotion/deployment that would apply migrations 005/006 to production requires separate exact Ron authorization.

capability_probes.assertion: A legacy Quest v1 event still reconstructs under the old contract and does not consume the Quest v2 player-focus slot.

After one ACTIVE Quest v2 exists, creation of a second Quest v2 is rejected in both JS and PostgreSQL, including concurrent DB creation guarded by one advisory player-slot lock; a terminal event frees the slot.
A structured Quest v2 cannot transition to COMPLETED while any required objective is below target.
FAILED/EXPIRED quests cannot later complete and therefore cannot become progression award bases.
Profile calibration, skills, achievements, shop and notification behavior remain unchanged by Quest v2.
Every Quest v2 state is reconstructable from ordered system_events and no mutable side table is introduced.

tests.expected: PASS: structured objectives/progress, reveal, fail/expire, deadlines, one-active-player focus and v1 compatibility.

PASS: hidden unrevealed quests are not player-rendered; objectives/rewards/deadline render; XP bar uses level-local progress.
PASS: legacy bridge remains recoverable and non-primary.
